correctness.rationale: The mask upper bound is immediate. For n<=2t+1, two identical symbols are at cyclic distance d<=t; deleting the intervening d−1 positions and exchanging which equal endpoint is removed yields two distinct t-deletion masks after t−d common exterior deletions (possible since n>=t+1). Thus short full shadows require pairwise distinct symbols, and the converse follows from surviving symbol sets. At any n, t unique markers plus period-(t+1) data with separate letters recover the deleted-marker set and anchor the circular output; retained index lists for r<=t deletions differ by <=r positionwise, so cannot match two equal data letters whose spacing is >=t+1. The critical n=2t+1 forces q>=2t+1, and n=2t+2 repeats the first data letter. The bundled verifier tests 60 construction parameter pairs/27113 masks, 4461 exhaustive critical words/44358 masks and three quaternary diagnostics; enumerations corroborate rather than prove all t,n.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparisons distinguish (a) source reconstruction from the set of cyclic subsequences, (b) stochastic trace complexity, (c) linear deletion-ball counting, and (d) rotation-orbit enumeration of special periodic sources. Remaining risk: unindexed equivalent constructions.
residual_risks: An unindexed marker-based full necklace shadow result or a stronger collision-free cyclic deletion embedding theorem could imply the present construction.

value.rationale: The number of deletion histories preserved by an origin-free circular readout is a natural channel ambiguity invariant. The theorem determines an all-deletion-count uniform alphabet threshold and a sharp change from forced pairwise-distinct sources to repeated-symbol full-shadow sources. It supplies a constructive all-length cyclic anchoring mechanism and a general short-arc obstruction not present in ordinary linear deletion balls, with potential use in testing combinatorial limits of circular storage traces; no unproved coding-capacity corollary is claimed.
